builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Toward a Scalable and Adaptive Evaluation Measure for Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: FastVUS replaces the standard VUS implementation (and the threshold-dependent Precision/Recall or threshold-independent AUC metrics VUS itself supersedes) with an exact reformulation using parallel buffer computation, buffer pruning, a single reduced matrix multiplication for the confusion matrix, one-pass buffer evaluation, and a global mask over non-anomalous regions; AutoVUS additionally replaces fixed buffer lengths with per-detection adaptive selection against a random baseline. The cost is negligible for constrained infrastructure: it is a CPU evaluation library with an optional GPU path that fits trivially in 24 GB, plus implementation complexity in adapting existing pipelines to the new API and validating the GPU variant's small approximation error. Failure modes include mis-ranking detectors if AutoVUS's random-baseline buffer selection behaves unexpectedly on datasets with unusual anomaly-length distributions, silent divergence of the approximate GPU path beyond its tested error bound, and wasted effort if the reader's production systems do not perform time series anomaly detection at all.
rationale: The method is open source and delivers a large, verified speedup in evaluation compute with no training cost, but it is only useful if the reader's production work involves time series anomaly detection.
technique: Fast and adaptive VUS metric for TSAD

claims.statement: FastVUS replaces the standard VUS implementation (and the threshold-dependent Precision/Recall or threshold-independent AUC metrics VUS itself supersedes) with an exact reformulation using parallel buffer computation, buffer pruning, a single reduced matrix multiplication for the confusion matrix, one-pass buffer evaluation, and a global mask over non-anomalous regions; AutoVUS additionally replaces fixed buffer lengths with per-detection adaptive selection against a random baseline. The cost is negligible for constrained infrastructure: it is a CPU evaluation library with an optional GPU path that fits trivially in 24 GB, plus implementation complexity in adapting existing pipelines to the new API and validating the GPU variant's small approximation error. Failure modes include mis-ranking detectors if AutoVUS's random-baseline buffer selection behaves unexpectedly on datasets with unusual anomaly-length distributions, silent divergence of the approximate GPU path beyond its tested error bound, and wasted effort if the reader's production systems do not perform time series anomaly detection at all.

FastVUS computes VUS exactly on average 76x faster than the reference implementation; the GPU variant reaches an average 304x speedup with a maximum numerical error of 5e-3, reducing evaluation of 32 detectors on 870 TSB-AD series from 7h38m to minutes.
